title: Docs: customer install/verify guide for signed offline bundles + internal support SOP
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: On-prem offline artifact signing (Private Deployment Automation)
body:
## Context
We’re introducing **signed offline bundles** for air-gapped installs of Redwood Private. This ticket covers:
1) Customer-facing guide: how to install + verify bundles fully offline (and what errors mean).
2) Internal support SOP: how SE/Support verifies bundles, collects diagnostics, and handles break-glass requests.

This work must align with the installer verification UX (fail-closed by default + explicit break-glass override with acknowledgement) and the security policy.

## Goals / deliverables
### A) Customer-facing documentation (public/enterprise-facing)
- "Installing Redwood Private using signed offline bundles" guide
  - prerequisites (supported OS, tooling, disk space, Kubernetes requirements)
  - expected bundle contents (images/charts/binaries/manifest/signature)
  - transfer guidance (USB/media/offline repo) + integrity caveats (don’t recompress/modify)
  - verify steps (recommended path) with commands + sample outputs
  - install steps (after verification) + recommended sequencing
  - upgrade/rollback notes (what’s allowed; when verification occurs)
  - FAQ: what is signed, what is verified, what keys are used, key rotation assurances

### B) Internal support SOP (Confluence/internal)
- "Support: troubleshooting offline bundle verification" SOP
  - how to triage common failure modes (signature invalid, manifest mismatch, missing artifacts, corrupted media)
  - log/diagnostic collection checklist
  - escalation path to Security + Release Eng
  - break-glass policy link + required customer acknowledgement language
  - how to confirm bundle provenance (release version, commit SHAs/build IDs)

## Source of truth / links
- Confluence: Offline bundles overview
  - https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/Offline+Bundles+Overview
- Confluence: Bundle format spec v1
  - https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/Offline+Bundle+Format+Spec+v1
- Confluence: Installer verification design
  - https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/Installer+Verification+Design
- Confluence: Runbook (verify offline bundle)
  - https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGPRIV/Runbook+-+Verify+Offline+Bundle
- Confluence: Break-glass policy
  - https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/SEC/Break-glass+Policy+-+Offline+Verification
- Linear (related)
  - ENG-3914: installer verify offline bundle signature
  - ENG-3915: break-glass override flow
  - ENG-3920: telemetry/audit logs for verification

## Target audience
- Primary: customer platform engineers / security engineers in regulated environments (air-gapped / offline)
- Secondary: Solutions Engineering, Support (L2/L3), Release Engineering on-call

## Requirements / constraints
- Must be **fully offline**: docs cannot require fetching keys, calling public endpoints, or online verification tools.
- Must be consistent with **fail-closed** behavior and the **explicit override** flow.
- Must not expose internal-only details (internal bucket paths, CI URLs, non-public key IDs, etc.).
- Must include a short section on **operational evidence**: what artifacts/logs customers can retain for audit.

## Proposed doc structure (customer guide)
1. Overview (what a signed offline bundle is; what it protects against)
2. What you received (bundle files + expected naming)
3. Pre-flight checks
   - verify checksums (if provided)
   - verify signature (required)
4. Installation
   - verify -> unpack -> load images -> install charts/manifests
   - recommended ordering + idempotency notes
5. Troubleshooting verification failures
   - signature verification failed
   - manifest digest mismatch
   - missing artifact referenced by manifest
   - clock/time issues (if any local checks exist)
6. Break-glass (emergency only)
   - what it does/doesn’t do
   - how it’s logged
   - when Support will allow it (link policy)
7. FAQ
   - key rotation + old bundle verification
   - downgrade protections (what’s enforced)
   - what changes invalidate a bundle

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Draft customer guide exists in `redwood-docs` (or customer docs workspace) and is reviewable by Product + Security.
- [ ] Internal support SOP is published in Confluence and linked from customer guide (where appropriate) and from Support onboarding.
- [ ] Includes copy/paste-able commands for verification and a sample of common error messages.
- [ ] Includes explicit section describing break-glass and required customer acknowledgement language (without encouraging use).
- [ ] Reviewed/approved by:
  - Security: Marcus Lin (content accuracy re: signing + break-glass policy)
  - Private Deployments Product: Vivek Kulkarni (customer messaging)
  - Support readiness: Dev Patel (triage checklist completeness)

## Open questions
- What is the final CLI surface for verification?
  - Waiting on ENG-3914/PR 1049 UX finalization (flags, exit codes, wording).
- Do we ship the public verification key in the bundle, or in the installer, or both?
  - Doc needs to match final key distribution plan.
- Should we include SBOM/provenance instructions in v1 doc or link to separate page?
  - Depends on ENG-3916 final approach.

## Notes
- Keep terminology consistent: "offline bundle", "bundle manifest", "detached signature", "verification".
- Avoid referencing internal-only systems (Linear/Jira links should be internal SOP only).
comments: 2025-02-11 — Vivek Kulkarni: Please include a short "what this protects against" section upfront. Customers keep asking about tampering during USB transfer and downgrade protection.
2025-02-12 — Marcus Lin: Make sure break-glass language matches policy doc exactly. Also add guidance that overrides must be recorded and shared back to Redwood Support for audit trail alignment.

2025-02-14 — Dev Patel: Add a diagnostics checklist: installer version, bundle version, verification command output, and the specific failing digest key from the manifest. Also call out that recompressing the bundle often changes file digests.

2025-02-18 — Kira Thompson: Draft outline is in progress; waiting for final CLI flags from ENG-3914/ENG-3915 to avoid churn in command examples. I’ll proceed with conceptual sections + placeholder commands and tighten after UX final.
